visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A man and a woman are in a modern, well-equipped gym. The woman, dressed in a beige t-shirt and black leggings, is performing tricep cable pull-downs using a rope attachment. Her face is obscured by a large, smiling cartoon mask overlay. Beside her, a man in a black tank top and white athletic shorts stands with his hand on the equipment, observing her form. (2) The scene shifts to the man performing a barbell bench press on a Smith machine. The woman stands at the head of the bench, acting as a spotter with her hands positioned near the barbell to provide safety. She continues to wear the cartoon mask. The lighting is bright and industrial, reflecting off the metal machinery. (3) The man stands behind the woman as she performs lateral raises with white dumbbells. He places his hands on her arms to guide her through the correct range of motion. They are positioned near a large window, allowing natural daylight to fill the space. (4) The man is now seated at a chest press machine. As he pushes the handles forward, the woman stands in front of him and places her hands on the handles, providing manual resistance or assistance. His facial expression shows physical exertion and a wide smile. (5) Transitioning to a mirror selfie, the woman holds her smartphone to capture a video of them. The cartoon mask is gone, revealing her real face. The man stands behind her, smiling broadly and flexing his well-developed biceps for the camera. The background shows treadmills and other gym equipment. (6) They are sitting cross-legged on a black foam mat on the floor. Both are holding large shaker bottles with prominent branding. They smile at each other, clink their bottles together in a toast, and take a sip. A smartphone and a small foam roller lie on the mat next to them. (7) The final shot is a static close-up of two Blender Bottle shakers placed on a circular glass table. One shaker is matte black and the other is a metallic bronze color, both featuring a distinct logo and the word 'MARS'.
